evidence.text: The -11.76% on 28 July was not a margin miss - margin ROSE to 11.1% from 11.0% - it was one unquantified paragraph: 'changes to the regulated mechanics of Demand Flexibility have begun to crystallise, and are expected to reduce recurring revenue per EV charger towards a more sustainable level early in the second half.' Demand Flexibility sits inside Energy Transition, which RBC sizes at ~11% of group sales but MORE THAN 20% of earnings, so the market de-rated ~20% of earnings on an unsized regulatory haircut. Tomorrow is the first disclosure with two months of post-change trading behind it, and the company has already twice said the change is 'consistent with the Board's expectations' while upgrading FY27 in the same announcement.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance upgrades at [THE COMPANY] have been paid: FY25 full-year TU 2026-01-29 +7.09%, FY25 results with the FY26 >GBP37m guide 2026-03-25 +8.40%, Q1 upgrade to >GBP40m 2026-05-19 +2.13%. Both prior interim results prints were positive: 2024-09-10 +2.35%, 2025-09-09 +9.46%. Across all 17 observed prints the mean is +2.53% and 10 of 17 are positive.

RTT News reported the fall with no explanation at all ('the article offers no analysis or commentary about the reason behind the share price drop'); MarketBeat's instant alert attributed it to 'the modest margin improvement... appears to have disappointed investors', which is factually backwards since the margin rose 10bp and the company said so in the same bullet. evidence.text: The one P&L line NOT pre-announced is adjusted PBT / adjusted EPS, and it should show a step change in optics. In H1 2026 net debt is flat YoY at GBP69.6m against GBP68.0m, so that step-up has annualised and UK rates have fallen. On a flat ~GBP3.0-3.1m finance charge, c.GBP15.8m of adjusted operating profit implies adjusted PBT of ~GBP12.7m (+17.6%) and adjusted EPS of ~6.8p (+15%) against last year's +3.5% - the earnings line growing FASTER than the pre-announced operating line, which is the reverse of last year.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025 interims printed adjusted EPS +3.5% against adjusted operating profit +9.5% - the weakest EPS/EBIT gap in the record - and the stock still rose 9.46%, so this shareholder base is not punitive on the EPS line. There is no instance in the 17-event record of the EPS line itself being the stated driver of a move.
evidence.why_not_priced: Every piece of wire copy and every broker summary I found quotes the pre-announced operating profit ('+14%') and none carries a PBT or EPS figure, because the trading update does not give one. The market's anchor for this print is therefore an EBIT number; the EPS number is the one that lands tomorrow and it is arithmetically better than the anchor. If this were priced you would see previews quoting an H1 EPS estimate - Deutsche Bank's 8 September preview, as reported, quotes revenue and divisional growth only. My PBT/EPS figures are MY estimate from two primary documents, clearly labelled, not a company number.
evidence.independence: Corroborated by the FY25 results RNS, which shows the same mechanism reversing over a full year once the debt annualised: adjusted operating profit +16.6% but adjusted EPS +20.0% - [url removed]

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No precedent on this name - Hornby ran it for the whole 17-event record, so there is no observation of how this shareholder base reacts to a CEO transition here. The CEO Retirement RNS (2026-06-15) and the Appointment RNS (2026-08-10) were both non-events for the tape: the stock closed 225p on 10 August against 226p on 7 August. That the appointment itself was a non-event is why the first-results risk is still live rather than already discharged.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a known fact with an unknown consequence, and the sell-side has priced the fact and not the consequence - Deutsche Bank upgraded to Buy on 8 September, a week after Muller started, on divisional growth forecasts that assume the inherited guidance holds. If the market were pricing reset risk you would expect the shares to have drifted DOWN into a new CEO's first print rather than up 9.3% in five sessions. I hold this as a fat left tail rather than a central case: three weeks is too short to kitchen-sink a half that was already pre-announced under the previous regime, and a strategic reset at a UK small cap normally waits for full-year results or a capital markets day.
evidence.independence: The departing founder-CEO sold 505,000 shares at 224.06p (~GBP1.13m) on 21 August 2026, two days before the 30-day closed period for a 22 September interim announcement would have begun - a timing detail visible only in the RNS, which points the same way on incentives - [url removed]

evidence.text: Bank net debt rose GBP17.3m in the half - from GBP52.3m at 31 December 2025 to GBP69.6m at 30 June 2026 - against a GBP0.6m FALL over the equivalent half of 2025. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Decisive, and it is why this is [sizing note removed].4 and not -1.5: at the 2025 interims bank net debt printed +72.6% YoY (GBP39.4m to GBP68.0m) and the stock rose 9.46% on the day. This shareholder base has demonstrably looked straight through a far larger balance-sheet expansion at this exact event. The FY24-to-FY25 pattern also shows the working capital reversing - adjusted free cash flow GBP3.5m in 2024 then GBP30.4m in 2025.
evidence.why_not_priced: Every summary of the July update I read - the AI abstract on Investegate, the Kalkine and Financial-News write-ups, the [url removed] piece - repeats the company's own YoY framing and none compares the GBP69.6m to the GBP52.3m the company itself published in March. But the lessons file is explicit that financing is a question, not a verdict, and the answer here is benign: the company says the money bought 'an investment in inventory ahead of the second half', and the H2 the guidance requires is exactly the ramp that inventory would serve. So this is an optic on the day, not a solvency point - leverage still fell to 1.5x, inside the 1-2x target range.
